title: npm can come from a different toolchain than the validated Node.js 22 executable
reasoning: The script validates one absolute Node.js executable but discovers and invokes npm independently through the original PATH. An earlier PATH directory can therefore supply an unrelated npm, causing installation failure or an unintended npm/Node pairing despite satisfying the Node.js requirement.
reproduction: Place a failing npm shim in an earlier PATH directory and a complete Node.js 22 toolchain later in PATH, ensure no compatible clawpatch exists, and run the installer. Node.js validation succeeds, but the unrelated npm handles npm pack.
recommendation: Resolve npm to an absolute path with node_dir prioritized, then invoke it with node_dir first in PATH so it uses the validated Node.js executable.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were linked for this installer feature, including mixed-toolchain PATH ordering.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run the installer with an unrelated npm earlier in PATH than a complete Node.js 22 toolchain and assert that the npm adjacent to the validated node is used.
minimumFixScope: Update npm resolution and both npm invocations in scripts/install.sh, then add one PATH-ordering regression test.

history.reasoning: The finding is fully revalidated. The stop hook is incompatible with the required strict-JSON response because valid JSON must end with `}` rather than a standalone completion line.
